column1: C++ bug: int overflow. What goes wrong?
column2: a * b with ints near 1e9; sums of 1e5 numbers up to 1e9. Fix: Use long long; write 1LL * a * b

column1: C++ bug: accumulate with 0. What goes wrong?
column2: accumulate(v.begin(), v.end(), 0) on long longs truncates. Fix: Pass 0LL

column1: C++ bug: Signed/unsigned loop. What goes wrong?
column2: for (int i = 0; i < v.size() - 1; i++) with an empty v: size() − 1 wraps to a huge value. Fix: Cast: (int)v.size() - 1

column1: C++ bug: Out-of-bounds index. What goes wrong?
column2: a[i + 1] at the last index; grid neighbours off the edge. Fix: Check bounds before indexing

column1: C++ bug: Uninitialised variables. What goes wrong?
column2: int ans; then ans = max(ans, x). Fix: Initialise every variable

column1: C++ bug: Global vs local arrays. What goes wrong?
column2: Large local array (1e6 ints) overflows the stack. Fix: Make it global or use vector

column1: C++ bug: Reset between test cases. What goes wrong?
column2: Globals or containers keep old data across t test cases. Fix: Clear or re-create per test

column1: C++ bug: endl in loops. What goes wrong?
column2: endl flushes every line: slow output. Fix: Use '\n'

column1: C++ bug: Slow I/O. What goes wrong?
column2: cin/cout without sync off on 1e6 numbers. Fix: ios::sync_with_stdio(false); cin.tie(nullptr);

column1: C++ bug: Mixing scanf and cin after sync off. What goes wrong?
column2: Undefined interleaving once sync is off. Fix: Use one style

column1: C++ bug: map[key] creates keys. What goes wrong?
column2: if (m[x]) inserts x and can grow the map in a loop. Fix: Use m.count(x) or m.find(x)

column1: C++ bug: Iterator invalidation. What goes wrong?
column2: Erasing from a vector or map while iterating with the same iterator. Fix: it = v.erase(it), or collect then erase

column1: C++ bug: Modifying a container in range-for. What goes wrong?
column2: push_back while iterating a vector. Fix: Iterate by index over the old size

column1: C++ bug: Comparator not strict. What goes wrong?
column2: sort with a <= b crashes or misorders. Fix: Comparators must be strict: a < b

column1: C++ bug: priority_queue order. What goes wrong?
column2: Expecting smallest on top. Fix: Default is max-heap; use greater<> for min

column1: C++ bug: multiset erase(value). What goes wrong?
column2: Removes every copy. Fix: erase(s.find(x)) to remove one

column1: C++ bug: Integer division and modulo with negatives. What goes wrong?
column2: -7 / 2 == -3 and -7 % 2 == -1. Fix: For a positive mod: ((a % m) + m) % m

column1: C++ bug: Modular arithmetic. What goes wrong?
column2: Forgetting % after each multiply. Fix: Reduce after every operation; use long long

column1: C++ bug: Floating point equality. What goes wrong?
column2: if (x == 0.3). Fix: Compare with an epsilon, or use integers

column1: C++ bug: pow() for integers. What goes wrong?
column2: pow(10, 9) returns double and can round down. Fix: Write a binary exponentiation for integers

column1: C++ bug: Wrong INF. What goes wrong?
column2: INT_MAX + 1 overflows during relaxations. Fix: Use 1e18 as long long or check before adding

column1: C++ bug: memset with non-zero values. What goes wrong?
column2: memset(a, 1, sizeof a) sets bytes, not ints. Fix: Only 0 and -1 are safe; use fill

column1: C++ bug: Recursion depth. What goes wrong?
column2: DFS 1e6 deep overflows the stack. Fix: Iterative DFS or BFS

column1: C++ bug: Passing big containers by value. What goes wrong?
column2: void f(vector<int> v) copies on every call. Fix: Pass by const reference

column1: C++ bug: string += in a loop with s = s + c. What goes wrong?
column2: s = s + c copies each time: O(n²). Fix: Use s += c or s.push_back(c)

column1: C++ bug: substr in a loop. What goes wrong?
column2: s.substr inside a loop copies: hidden O(n²). Fix: Use indices or string_view

column1: C++ bug: Off-by-one in binary search. What goes wrong?
column2: while (lo < hi) with mid rounding the wrong way loops forever. Fix: Pick one template and stick to it

column1: C++ bug: Shadowed variables. What goes wrong?
column2: Declaring n again inside a block hides the outer n. Fix: Compile with -Wall -Wshadow

column1: C++ bug: Edge cases. What goes wrong?
column2: n = 1, empty input, all equal, all negative, maximum values. Fix: Test them before submitting

column1: C++ bug: Reading the wrong constraints. What goes wrong?
column2: O(n²) for n = 2e5. Fix: From n, decide the target complexity first
